The top layer has one number 2; the next layer has two number 0s; the layer after that has three number 0s; the bottom layer has four number 6s. The arrows of each node all point downward to one or two adjacent nodes in the next layer. Then reason: To obtain the number 2006, one needs to follow the arrows starting from the top 2, pass through two layers of 0s, and finally reach a 6 at the bottom. That is, count the number of directed paths from the top vertex to any 6 in the bottom layer. Count layer by layer: the top 2 has 1 way to arrive; the two 0s in the second layer have 1 and 1 ways respectively; the three 0s in the third layer have 1, 2, and 1 ways respectively; the four 6s in the bottom layer have 1, 3, 3, and 1 ways respectively. Therefore the total is 1+3+3+1=8.

method.method_draft: Read the figure as a layered directed graph: the top node is labeled 2, the next layer has two nodes labeled 0, the next layer has three nodes labeled 0, and the bottom layer has four nodes labeled 6. The arrows always go downward from a node to one of the two adjacent nodes in the next layer. The text asks for the number of ways to obtain 2006, so a valid way is any directed path from the top 2 through one 0 in each of the next two layers and ending at a 6. Count paths layer by layer: from the top there is 1 way; the two first-zero nodes receive 1 and 1 way; the three second-zero nodes receive 1, 2, and 1 ways; the four bottom 6 nodes receive 1, 3, 3, and 1 ways. Sum the ways ending at any bottom 6: 1+3+3+1=8.
